stories.name: Netflix analyst downgrades
stories.blurb: Wells Fargo and other Wall Street analysts are cutting Netflix's price targets and downgrading its stock over worries about weak viewer engagement and content.

stories.name: Netflix Q2 earnings selloff
stories.blurb: Netflix shares fell sharply after the company's second-quarter revenue missed expectations and its third-quarter guidance came in weaker than investors had hoped.

events.name: Ackman's Pershing Square buys Netflix stake
Q2 revenue miss, weak Q3 guidance
Wells Fargo downgrades Netflix, cuts target

8.text: Netflix shares fell over 14% in September, nearing July’s $65 low. HSBC cut its 2026 target, citing a widening viewing gap and a slipping edge over rivals.

6.text: Wells Fargo and HSBC downgraded Netflix, citing declining viewer engagement, weak original content, and YouTube's growing share of TV viewing. HSBC cut its rating to Hold and price target to $76, and the stock fell about 8.7%.

4.text: YouTube is adding production tools to keep creators from leaving for Netflix, which is poaching popular channels. The articles frame YouTube as a growing competitive threat to Netflix.

5.text: Netflix shares fell over 20% in 2026 amid slowing revenue growth—decelerating to 13.4% in Q2 with roughly 12% forecast for Q3—and rising competition. Analysts remain largely bullish nonetheless, citing cheap valuation and ad/price-hike potential, though price targets diverge widely ($70–$135).

7.text: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square has repurchased roughly $1 billion in Netflix stock, the same position it sold in June at a $400 million loss. Investor Steve Weiss also said on September 23 that he added to his Netflix position after the stock fell 42% over the year.
